messages:
jordan_customer: Hey team — ACME is hitting a Safari-only issue with streaming (EventSource). They get a few messages then the stream stops delivering mid-response. Chrome/FF OK. Happening through their CDN (Akamai). Customer says it started after they enabled edge caching rules. Repro steps and headers below.
anna_support: Thanks Jordan — can you paste a minimal repro + the request id or sample response headers? Is this using our hosted API or Dedicated? Any error IDs from the SDK?
jordan_customer: Hosted API, region=us-west. No SDK error id shown in browser. Repro steps: 1) open page in Safari 16.6 2) connect EventSource to /v1/streams with Authorization header 3) occasionally stream yields partial chunk then onerror fires and no reconnect. I attached curl output:

```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/streamid
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Cache-Control: max-age=0, must-revalidate
ETag: "abc123"
Vary: Authorization

: first comment
data: {"id":1,"text":"hello"}

# then connection stops receiving further data client-side
```

And when the edge returns a 304 on a revalidation it looks like:

```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Cache-Control: max-age=0
Age: 0
Vary: Authorization
```

Safari console shows: "EventSource failed to connect" then no further events. They are using eventsource-polyfill to support older mobile webviews.
mike_eng: This reads like an edge caching + Safari revalidation interaction. Safari's EventSource can treat a 304 or unexpected revalidation midstream as terminal in some cases. If the edge returns 304 for the same connection or tries to revalidate a range, the browser may drop the socket. Also worrying: ETag + Vary: Authorization on a streaming endpoint is risky.
li_infra: Can we get the exact request id or edge logs for one of the failed sessions? I want to see if the edge is returning a 304 while the origin is still streaming. If the edge sees a conditional GET mid-connection that could close the upstream keepalive and present a 304 to the client which Safari mishandles.
jordan_customer: Pasted a small browser log snippet — when it fails we see repeated preflight / revalidate calls from Akamai in the network tab, then the EventSource onerror fires. Only Safari.
jess_devex: Suggested quick customer mitigation:
- Turn off edge caching for SSE endpoints. Add Cache-Control: no-store or private, no-transform.
- Remove ETag/Last-Modified for streaming responses; they invite revalidation.
- Ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked and avoid final Content-Length header.
- Add periodic SSE comment heartbeats (":\n\n") every ~15s to keep intermediaries from timing out.
- If they must keep caching, make the endpoint set "Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate" and Vary: Authorization only when strictly necessary (but for SSE we usually avoid caching entirely).
mike_eng: Agreed. From a product-side fix we should ensure our streaming router sets these headers by default. We can also strip ETag on streaming routes and set X-Accel-Buffering: no for nginx origins. I'll file a fix to force Cache-Control: private, no-transform and drop ETag for /v1/streams/*.
li_infra: Workaround for customers who can't change CDN rules: recommend switching token transport temporarily to short-lived signed query param (if their CDN doesn't strip those) or use a cookie with same-site settings. Not ideal security-wise but useful for triage.
jordan_customer: Will try turning off Akamai caching for the endpoint and report back. One more thing — they rely on eventsource-polyfill for older iOS webviews. Could the polyfill be making this worse?
mike_eng: Possibly. Polyfills open an XHR/long-poll fallback in some implementations; those will definitely be affected by 304s and caching. Native EventSource/streams are still subject to Safari quirks but are less likely to interpret a midstream 304 as success. Ask the customer to test in Safari w/o polyfill (if possible) to isolate.
jess_devex: Example header snippet to give to customer/edge engineers:

```
# recommended origin response headers for SSE
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, private
Pragma: no-cache
Vary: none
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
X-Accel-Buffering: no
```

Also recommend adding a keepalive ping: `: ping\n\n` every 12s.

anna_support: I'll summarize for the customer and request permission to look at edge logs. If they want a fast workaround we can issue them a support token with a different transport in the short term. @deploy-bot can you open an internal incident/ticket to track the front-end routing change to force no-cache on streams?

deploy-bot: Created ticket INC-2026-239: "SSE: force no-cache and drop ETag on streaming routes". Assignee: mike_eng. Link: https://rwd.incidents/INC-2026-239
mike_eng: I'll pick this up. Plan: 1) add header enforcement in streaming router 2) roll to staging 3) ask infra to propagate guidance to CDN configs 4) follow up with the customer. ETA for patch: today evening PST.
jordan_customer: Thanks — I've asked ACME to disable caching for the route and to test without the polyfill. I'll update once they test. Appreciate the quick response :heart:!

anna_support: Thx Jordan. If ACME confirms it's fixed after disabling cache we'll mark resolved and offer a credit for the interruption. Please paste the client-side network HAR if it recurs so infra can correlate.
mike_eng: Note for the team: long-term we should detect when an intermediate 304 or revalidation happens on a stream and emit a structured log/event so we can alert on increased revalidation counts. Filed as follow-up on INC-2026-239.
